UI · 8/27 · THE BOHEMIA LOOK

Your look is in the game now, not on this page. These are photographs of the real run on a real phone screen, before and after. Thumb anything you hate.

THE CONVERSATION

Same words, same person, same moment in the quest. Your three answers used to be soft grey slabs in a font the game never loaded. Now they are cut at the corner, outlined at two pixels, and gold, because gold means you.

PRESSED, THE ONE YOU JUST PICKED

You voted FLIP this afternoon and it is already in the game. The whole button turns solid gold, not just the middle, because the middle is where your thumb is.

THE LINE AT THE TOP

What you are doing is gold. Where you are is blue-green, because the game is telling you that, you did not choose it. That split is the whole of your colour pick.

THE EIGHT ARROWS

These used to be eight letters borrowed from whatever font your phone had. No font has all eight arrows, so four came out thin and four came out fat, in the same ring. They are drawn now. One shape, eight turns, identical forever.

Four of the seven are decided and this page is wearing them. Everything you see below and above is already your choice, not a sample. Two are dead because you said no to all of them, and I did not cook you replacements. One is left, and it is the one you could not see, so now it plays itself.

YOUR GAME, WEARING WHAT YOU CHOSE

ANYTHING ELSE

Two games taken apart: Final Fantasy 10, and Machine Party. Not a list of things I like about them. 32 things they do, why each one works, and what Bohemia does about it. 8 of them we cannot have, and those are the useful ones.

You said it is Final Fantasy 10 meets Machine Party. That is the last card in this list and it is the only thing here that is a decision rather than a note. Read it and tell me if I got your sentence right.

32things found 15we take 9we change 8we cannot have

A study where everything is worth stealing is not a study, it is a fan page. Final Fantasy X is a TV game, played with a controller, with seven people in your party, in a hallway, with real actors reading the lines. We are a phone game, one thumb, one person, an open city, and nobody reads anything out loud. A lot of what makes it great is paid for by things we do not have.

LOOK material, colour, type, shape

FFX.L01 ADAPT

THE MENU IS A PANE OF GLASS LAID ON THE WORLD

Every FFX panel is a translucent deep-indigo box with a thin light border and a soft inner gradient, drawn over the live scene. The world keeps moving behind it. The menu never replaces the picture, it is laid on top of it.

WHY IT WORKS The interface reads as an OBJECT with a material, not as a document. And because the world stays visible, opening a menu never feels like leaving.

ADAPT · WHAT WE DO Bohemia's fork 5 (THE DIRT) is the same idea in a different material. FFX's interface is made of glass; ours would be made of a dirty steel plate. Both say the same thing: the interface is a thing, not a page.

CAREFUL DO NOT COPY THE TRANSLUCENCY. FFX gets away with glass because its battle backgrounds are low-contrast and softly lit. Bohemia's world is high-contrast pixel art at 1:1, and text over it at 40% opacity is unreadable. Opaque plate, grime on the plate, world visible AROUND it, never THROUGH it.

looked at through: clarity (Hodent) · the geometry axis (Fagerholt & Lorentzon) · seen on: battle, main menu, shop

FFX.L02 TAKE

ONE FACE, AND IT WAS CARRYING MORE THAN ANYONE KNEW

One typeface across the entire game, in one weight, at essentially two sizes. The 2013 HD Remaster changed that typeface and the menu cursor and almost nothing else material. Ten years later players still say the remaster damaged the game, and the type is the thing they name.

WHY IT WORKS A typeface is not decoration in a game with this much reading. It is the voice the game speaks in. Swap it and the same words sound like someone else.

TAKE · WHAT WE DO MEASURED 8/26: BOHEMIA HAS NO TYPEFACE. The alpha asks for one called Space Grotesk in exactly one place, never loads it, and has no font file. Every letter in the build is whatever the phone decided. That is what makes fork 4 on the UI page a real decision and not a cosmetic one.

looked at through: consistency (Hodent) · seen on: everywhere

FFX.L03 TAKE

THE INTERFACE LIVES IN A HUE THE WORLD DOES NOT USE

Spira is tropical, turquoise water, wet sand, green, warm skin. The menus are deep indigo, a value and a hue the world barely touches. The interface and the world are never competing for the same part of the eye.

WHY IT WORKS Separation by HUE costs nothing and works before you read a single word.

TAKE · WHAT WE DO This answers fork 3 from inside his own favourite game. Bohemia's world is desert tan and GOLD LIGHT, and LIGHT = TERRITORY is law: gold means a lamp is on and somebody owns that ground. If the buttons are gold too, gold stops meaning light. The UI has to live where the world does not, which is the argument for BONE.

looked at through: clarity (Hodent) · seen on: everywhere

FFX.L04 REFUSE

THE NUMBERS ARE BIG AND THEY FLY

Damage pops off the target in a large face, arcs upward, and fades. 9999 is a landmark players chase for a hundred hours.

WHY IT WORKS The feedback is bigger than the event. That is deliberate: a hit you can barely see reads as a hit that barely happened.

REFUSE · WHAT WE DO NO DAMAGE BEFORE THE DIAL is our own law and it is not negotiable. The SHAPE is banked for the day the dial exists; the content waits. Recording it here so nobody has to rediscover it, and so nobody ships it early.

looked at through: signs and feedback (Hodent) · meta UI (Fagerholt & Lorentzon) · seen on: battle

FFX.L05 ADAPT

THE INTERFACE MOVES IN AND OUT INSTEAD OF CUTTING

FFX slides its panels in and out. It very rarely hard-cuts from one screen state to another, and on a 2001 console it holds that even across the cutscene-to-battle handoff.

WHY IT WORKS A transition that MOVES reads as faster than a cut that waits, even when the clock says otherwise. Motion tells you the machine is alive.

ADAPT · WHAT WE DO Playtest dispatch item 7 is "THE GAME KINDA RUNS LIKE SHIT", measured at 24.2 seconds to first play on throttled 4G. Some of that is real load and needs real optimisation, which is RUN's. But some of the FEELING is that our panels appear rather than arrive. That half is this lane's and it is cheap.

CAREFUL motion has a budget on a phone and this lane does not get to spend RUN's frame time. Transform and opacity only, never layout.

looked at through: consistency (Hodent) · seen on: battle entry, menu open, cutscene handoff

MP.L01 REFUSE

THE GRIME CROSSES THE SEAM, AND THAT IS WHY IT IS ONE PLACE

Klubnika on texturing: he "added dirty and grimy leaks to every corner, which blends everything together rather than having different objects." One filth pass laid over everything, indifferent to where one object stops and the next begins.

WHY IT WORKS A wall, a floor and a machine that share a stain are one building. Three surfaces each perfectly textured that share nothing are three assets. The dirt, not the palette, is what makes a room read as a place.

REFUSE · WHAT WE DO He killed all three dirt options on the UI page on 8/27, and that is not a contradiction of this finding, it is a correction of where I aimed it. Klubnika's grime unifies THE ROOM YOU ARE STANDING IN. I took a world technique and put it on a menu, which is the one surface in the game that is NOT part of the room. The interface is not another object in the scene, it is the sheet of instructions laid over the scene, and dirtying it makes it look like a texture that failed rather than a thing that has been used. THE FINDING IS GOOD AND IT BELONGS TO THE WORLD LANE, WHERE THE GRIME SHEET IS ALREADY WIRED AT HIS RULED 0.30. It does not belong on his buttons and he was right to say so.

looked at through: consistency (Hodent) - the mechanism behind "it reads as one room" · seen on: the world

MP.L02 TAKE

EVERYTHING IS THICK

The interface objects are deliberately CHUNKY. Heavy metal shapes, thick edges, industrial smoke, club light reflecting off the gun. Nothing in his work is a hairline.

WHY IT WORKS A thick thing reads at a glance and reads in bad light. It also reads as MADE, out of steel, by somebody who was not thinking about elegance.

TAKE · WHAT WE DO This is the fork he answered on 8/27. He said yes to the HEAVY line, 2px at 3.78 to 1 against the panel, and no to the hairline that measured 1.22. His vote and Klubnika's steel are the same instinct, and the number now says so.

looked at through: form follows function (Hodent) - clarity (Hodent) · seen on: the table, the gun, the terminal

MP.L03 REFUSE

THE TEXTURES ARE PHOTOGRAPHS OF REAL THINGS

He photographs his own textures, mainly of electronics, and urban-explores abandoned factories for reference. The Volta electrical component facility in Tallinn, which he went back to "a dozen times".

WHY IT WORKS Photographic surfaces are uncorrelated at the finest scale, which is a thing you can measure. It is why his rooms feel like rooms instead of like materials.

REFUSE · WHAT WE DO Bohemia is 44px three-quarter pixel art on a phone and a photograph pasted into that is mush. But the finding explains something already measured here: his bought tile library reads edge 18.4 and grain 61% where painted art reads 9.4 and 26%, and the reason is that photographs ARE uncorrelated at the pixel. HIM LOVING THIS LOOK AND HIM BUYING THAT LIBRARY ARE THE SAME TASTE POINTING AT THE SAME PHYSICAL PROPERTY. The technique cannot come. The measurement it explains is already in the world lane's hands.

looked at through: clarity (Hodent) - the geometry axis (Fagerholt & Lorentzon) · seen on: every surface

MP.L04 ADAPT

THE ROOM IS MADE OF THREE MATERIALS AND NO MORE

Concrete, steel, and a sick electric light. His environments are brutalist and the palette is what the building is physically made of, not a colour scheme chosen on top of it.

WHY IT WORKS When the palette IS the material list, nothing on screen can be off-model, because every colour has a reason you could point at in the world.

ADAPT · WHAT WE DO Bohemia's world is desert tan and gold light, and LIGHT = TERRITORY says the gold means somebody is keeping a lamp on. So our material list is already written: sun-bleached tan, dead concrete, and the gold of the few lights left. What ports is the discipline, not the colours: the interface may only use what the valley is made of, plus the one cold that the valley does NOT have, which is what he chose on 8/27 for exactly this reason.

looked at through: consistency (Hodent) · seen on: every screen

READ what it tells you, and how fast

FFX.R01 TAKE

THE FUTURE IS ON SCREEN

The CTB window is a stack of portraits along the upper right showing WHO ACTS NEXT, in order, several turns ahead. It is not a bar you interpret. It is a LIST you read.

WHY IT WORKS FFX runs a hidden simulation, agility, action rank, tick counters. Instead of teaching the player that arithmetic, it does the arithmetic and shows THE ANSWER. The player never computes anything and still plans four moves out.

TAKE · WHAT WE DO Bohemia is I-MOVE-YOU-MOVE on a 120 BPM clock, and combat is "Rogue Fable 4 with 120 BPM everything". The beat is the clock the turns run on. Right now that clock is a FELT thing with no picture: the player hears it and never sees who the next few beats belong to. FFX has the exact answer, shipped in 2001, and we already have the data to fill it.

CAREFUL FFX's list is a tall column on the right of a 4:3 screen. On an iPhone in portrait the right edge is where the thumb lives (SHARED -5). Ours has to run along the TOP, or be short enough not to reach into the thumb.

looked at through: signs and feedback + minimum workload (Hodent) · seen on: battle

FFX.R02 TAKE

THE PREVIEW IS THE TUTORIAL

The turn list RE-SORTS LIVE while you are still choosing. Move the cursor onto a slow, heavy ability and watch your own portrait slide further down. Hover Slow and watch the enemy's icons fall.

WHY IT WORKS The rule "weaker abilities cost less cooldown" is never written down anywhere. It is DEMONSTRATED, for free, every time the player compares two commands. The system teaches itself by being visible.

TAKE · WHAT WE DO Every Bohemia ability that costs beats should show its cost as a change in the beat list BEFORE the player commits, not as a number in a tooltip and not as a surprise afterwards. This is also how the 60 mini-boss abilities get taught without sixty tutorials.

looked at through: form follows function (Hodent) · seen on: battle

FFX.R03 ADAPT

THE COMMAND LIST IS THE CHARACTER SHEET

Every character's command menu is DIFFERENT. Rikku has Steal and Use. Auron has Break. Kimahri has Lancet. You learn who somebody is by reading what their menu offers, before you ever read a stat.

WHY IT WORKS The menu is not a list of buttons, it is a portrait. Identity is expressed in what a person is ALLOWED to do.

ADAPT · WHAT WE DO THERE ARE NO RUNS and there is ONE character for a hundred hours, so a menu cannot tell people apart here, there is only him. But the same law says 60 MINI BOSSES each hand you A NEW WAY TO INTERACT WITH BOHEMIA. So the action list IS the experience tree made visible: what you can do is what you have beaten. The menu stops being a control panel and becomes a trophy case, and it grows for a hundred hours.

looked at through: form follows function (Hodent) · seen on: battle

FFX.R04 TAKE

THE MENU REMEMBERS WHERE YOU WERE

The cursor returns to the last thing you chose. Attack stays under the cursor. The item you used last time is where you left it.

WHY IT WORKS In a game with thousands of menu openings, one saved keypress each is a measurable amount of a player's life. Nobody ever notices this working. Every player notices it missing.

TAKE · WHAT WE DO Cheap, invisible, and the demo will have people opening the phone and the action list hundreds of times in twenty minutes.

looked at through: minimum workload (Hodent) · seen on: battle, item list, shop

FFX.R05 TAKE

THE READOUT SAYS WHAT IT DOES, NOT WHAT IT IS

Selecting a target names it and shows the consequence in the same breath, the enemy's name, and whether this will help or hurt. The information appears at the moment of the decision, not in a screen you have to go find.

WHY IT WORKS Information delivered late is information the player has to REMEMBER, and memory is the most expensive thing a UI can spend.

TAKE · WHAT WE DO Directly serves NO ESSENTIAL INFORMATION BY COLOUR ALONE and its sister rule for sound: if the consequence is written at the point of decision, the player never has to have heard or seen a cue they missed.

looked at through: clarity (Hodent) · Pinelle/Wong/Stach (heuristics mined from what players actually complained about across 108 games) · seen on: battle target select, item list

MP.R01 TAKE

TELL THEM THE COUNT. HIDE ONLY THE ORDER.

Buckshot Roulette loads the shotgun in front of you and TELLS YOU EXACTLY how many live rounds and how many blanks are going in. What it never tells you is the ORDER. Two live and three blanks, and no idea which one is next.

WHY IT WORKS THIS IS THE BEST INFORMATION DESIGN IN EITHER GAME IN THIS BOOK. Complete information about the composition, zero information about the sequence. Nothing is hidden to create difficulty, so the player never feels cheated, and yet every single pull is a real decision. Hiding the count would make it a coin flip. Showing the order would make it arithmetic. He hides exactly one thing.

TAKE · WHAT WE DO Final Fantasy 10 showed us DO THE ARITHMETIC AND SHOW THE ANSWER. Machine Party shows us WHICH ONE THING TO WITHHOLD. Together they are a rule Bohemia can hold every screen against: the player should know everything about WHAT IS IN THE ROOM and nothing about WHICH ORDER IT COMES IN. A district that tells you it holds four dogs and a man with a pipe, without telling you what is around the next corner, is Valheim-style danger by place done the honest way, and it is the exact opposite of a health bar that hides its own number.

looked at through: signs and feedback (Hodent) - minimum workload (Hodent) · seen on: the table

MP.R02 TAKE

YOUR LIFE IS A COUNT OF CHARGES, NOT A NUMBER

Health in Buckshot Roulette is a DEFIBRILLATOR with charges, shown as lightning bolts. Two, three or four. Take a live round to the head and you spend a charge. There is no bar and no percentage.

WHY IT WORKS A small countable thing is read instantly and felt physically. Nobody has to translate 62% into "how many more mistakes do I get". Three bolts means three mistakes, and the answer arrives before you have finished looking.

TAKE · WHAT WE DO NO DAMAGE BEFORE THE DIAL is our law, so the numbers wait, but the SHAPE is free and it is a decision the health readout has to make anyway. A countable charge also survives the thumb rule: three big marks read at a glance in the corner of a phone, where a thin bar with a number in it does not.

looked at through: form follows function (Hodent) - diegetic (Fagerholt & Lorentzon) · seen on: the table

MP.R03 REFUSE

THERE IS NO HUD, BECAUSE THE MACHINE IS ALREADY IN FRONT OF YOU

Buckshot Roulette is described as "diegetic systems and minimal UI", and s.p.l.i.t goes further: the entire game takes place inside a working terminal, with no HUD elements at all to break the illusion of sitting at the machine.

WHY IT WORKS He can delete the HUD because a first-person camera puts a real object at arm's length, and the object carries the information on its own face.

REFUSE · WHAT WE DO Final Fantasy 10 could delete its HUD because it is a corridor (FFX.W03). Klubnika can delete his because the machine is at arm's length in first person. BOHEMIA HAS NEITHER EXCUSE. We are three-quarter view at 44px in an open valley of 27 districts, and he has already reported walking through it lost. Two of the greatest interfaces we have studied both have almost no interface, AND BOTH OF THEM PAID FOR IT WITH SOMETHING WE DO NOT HAVE. That is not a coincidence to admire, it is a bill to notice. We earn a quiet screen with landmarks and light, or we do not get one.

looked at through: non-diegetic minimisation (Fagerholt & Lorentzon) - diegetic (same) · seen on: every screen

MP.R04 ADAPT

NOTHING WAITS

Klubnika's stated design rule for Machine Party: "no fluff, no waiting, just back to back violent chaos." He says they cut down the dialogue, the transitions, and the board-game bits that minigame collections usually carry.

WHY IT WORKS The connective tissue is where players quit, and it is invisible to the person who built it because they are proud of it.

ADAPT · WHAT WE DO Bohemia is a hundred hours and a single character, so it cannot be back to back chaos and should not try. What ports is the AUDIT: every screen between him and the next decision is on trial. Measured already, the run takes 24.2 seconds to first play on throttled 4G and he told us the game "kinda runs like shit". That is the same complaint in his words, and it is a demo blocker.

looked at through: minimum workload (Hodent) - Pinelle/Wong/Stach, built from what players actually complain about · seen on: between everything

DO pressing, aiming, taking it back

FFX.D01 REFUSE

NO CLOCK MEANS NO PANIC, AND THAT IS WHAT MAKES THE LIST READABLE

CTB replaced the series' Active Time Battle. The world PAUSES on your turn and you have an indefinite period of time to choose.

WHY IT WORKS This is the finding under the finding. FFX's famous turn preview only works because there is time to read it. A preview you have no time to read is decoration. Square did not add a preview to ATB; they removed the timer FIRST.

REFUSE · WHAT WE DO Bohemia is 120 BPM and EVERYTHING QUANTIZES TO THE BEAT. We want FFX's readable list while running something closer to ATB's clock. That is a real tension and pretending it is not is how a study becomes a fan page. WHAT THIS LANE THINKS, ROUTED, NOT DECIDED: the beat should be the METRONOME, not the shot clock. I-MOVE-YOU-MOVE already says the world advances when you act. If standing still costs nothing, the player has all the time in the world to read the list, and the beat only decides WHEN the action lands, not how long you get to think. That keeps both. It is COMBAT's and RUN's call, not mine.

looked at through: user control and flexibility (Hodent) · seen on: battle

FFX.D02 TAKE

TARGETING IS A SENTENCE, AND YOU CAN STOP HALFWAY

Choose a verb, and only then the valid targets light up and an arrow bobs over the current one. Circle commits, Triangle backs out, at every step.

WHY IT WORKS The mistake is caught before it costs anything. Two steps and a cancel is the cheapest error-prevention there is, and it is why nobody has ever rage-quit FFX for hitting the wrong thing.

TAKE · WHAT WE DO UI-2 says THE ACTION BUTTON DOES ACTIONS AND NEVER CHANGES MEANING. A verb-then-target with a visible way out is exactly the shape that keeps that promise: the button always means "do the thing I have picked", and picking is reversible until the moment it is not.

looked at through: error prevention and error recovery (Hodent) · seen on: battle

FFX.D03 ADAPT

THE SWAP IS FREE, BUT IT IS SCOPED

On a character's turn you can swap them out for anyone on the bench with one button, at no cost in turns. But ONLY the character whose turn it is can be swapped. You cannot stand there cycling the whole roster for free.

WHY IT WORKS A generous affordance with one honest limit. It puts the entire seven-person cast into every fight without a party-management screen and without letting the player abuse it.

ADAPT · WHAT WE DO THERE ARE NO RUNS and there is no party, so the letter of it cannot come. The shape lands on the experience tree: the 60 mini bosses each hand you a new way to interact with Bohemia, and a hundred-hour kit needs a way to change what is ready WITHOUT a loadout screen. FFX's answer is the one to copy, the change is free, but only on the beat you were about to spend anyway, and only to the slot you were about to spend it on. No pause menu, no cost, no abuse.

looked at through: minimum workload + error prevention (Hodent) · seen on: battle

FFX.D04 TAKE

THE BIG VERB IS EARNED BY A VERB YOU CHOOSE

Overdrive is a per-character gauge sitting next to their HP that fills from what HAPPENS, then unlocks one big move. And Overdrive MODES let the player choose WHICH event charges it, taking damage, an ally taking damage, healing, and so on. You pick what your power is made of.

WHY IT WORKS The gauge is not a timer. It is a record of how you have been playing.

TAKE · WHAT WE DO THE LAW SAYS IT IN OUR OWN WORDS, "a real kit of abilities recharged by VERBS, not timers" (8/26, THERE ARE NO RUNS). His favourite game shipped that exact idea in 2001 and we did not notice it was already solved. Overdrive Modes are the closest thing in any Final Fantasy to the rule we wrote down this week.

looked at through: form follows function (Hodent) · seen on: battle, character menu

MP.D01 REFUSE

THE MACHINE IS THE INTERFACE

Across his whole catalogue the interface is the thing in front of you: terminals, keys, switches, panels. s.p.l.i.t is "raw keyboard-driven interactions, terminal-based puzzles". The tension comes from OPERATING A MACHINE, not from reading a HUD laid over one.

WHY IT WORKS A machine has weight, sequence and consequence. A menu has none of those; it has options. Operating something is dramatic in a way choosing something is not.

REFUSE · WHAT WE DO There is no "in front of you" in a three-quarter top-down game on a phone. The camera looks DOWN at a character; it never looks AT an object at arm's length, so a diegetic terminal has nowhere to be. Anyone who reads "Final Fantasy 10 meets Machine Party" and starts drawing a first-person control panel has copied the thing that cannot come and skipped the four that can. What survives the port is one sentence of it, and it is MP.D02 and MP.D03 below.

looked at through: diegetic (Fagerholt & Lorentzon) - form follows function (Hodent) · seen on: every screen

MP.D02 TAKE

DESIGNED FOR A PURPOSE, WITH NO THOUGHT FOR THE USER

On the machines in Buckshot Roulette: everything is built to do one specific job and nothing about it was shaped for a human hand.

WHY IT WORKS It is a rule you can hold an object against and get a straight yes or no, which almost no aesthetic note manages. It is also the whole difference between industrial-LOOKING and industrial.

TAKE · WHAT WE DO Post-economic-apocalypse Las Vegas is full of machinery that outlived the people it was for, which is the same sentence from the other end. Hold every object in the valley against it: was this shaped for a hand, or shaped for a job? A parking meter, a fare box, a slot machine and a fuel pump all answer the second way, and all four are already in the districts. It is a test the world lane can run today without cooking anything.

looked at through: form follows function (Hodent), inverted on purpose · seen on: every object

MP.D03 ADAPT

YOU OPERATE IT, YOU DO NOT COMMAND IT

You do not select "shoot dealer" off a list. You pick the gun up, you point it, and you pull. The verb is carried out with your hands in stages, and each stage is a place you could still stop.

WHY IT WORKS Stages make the decision feel like yours. A one-tap command from a menu is over before it is felt.

ADAPT · WHAT WE DO Final Fantasy 10 already gave us the phone-sized version of this in FFX.D02: pick the verb, THEN pick the target, and back out at any point. That is operating in two stages with a way to stop, on a touchscreen, and the action button never changes what it means (UI-2). Klubnika's version is why that shape is worth keeping rather than collapsing into one tap for speed.

looked at through: user control and flexibility (Hodent) - error prevention (Hodent) · seen on: the table

WORLD where the menu touches the story

FFX.W01 TAKE

THE SAVE POINT IS A THING YOU WALK TO

A Save Sphere is a glowing object standing in the world. You walk to it and touch it. It saves, it heals, and its presence is a warning: something is about to happen, this is the last quiet place.

WHY IT WORKS One object doing four jobs, a save, a heal, a landmark, and a held breath, and it costs zero screen space because it IS the screen.

TAKE · WHAT WE DO Bohemia already puts SLEEP (8 HOURS, SAVES) on the action button. Making the save a PLACE instead of a menu row is more Bohemia than any menu will ever be, and it wires straight into two other rulings: DANGER BY PLACE (Valheim-style district tiers) and LIGHT = TERRITORY. A place you can save is a place somebody is keeping the lights on. The safe map and the light map become the same map.

looked at through: diegetic UI (Fagerholt & Lorentzon: inside the fiction AND inside the geometry) · signs and feedback (Hodent) · seen on: the world

FFX.W02 ADAPT

THE INTERFACE TEACHES YOU A LANGUAGE, ONE LETTER AT A TIME

Al Bhed characters speak in what looks like gibberish. Scattered across the world are Al Bhed Primers, and each one you find permanently decodes ONE LETTER, everywhere, retroactively, for the rest of the game. Your interface literally becomes more legible the longer you play.

WHY IT WORKS Comprehension as progression. Nothing else in the medium does this. It makes a hundred-hour game reward attention with UNDERSTANDING rather than with stats.

ADAPT · WHAT WE DO THEY SPEAK SPANGLISH (8/25, LOCKED) and that law has a hard rule inside it: LANGUAGE NEVER GATES REQUIRED INFORMATION. FFX's version DOES gate information behind language, that is the whole mechanic. So we cannot take it as built. HIS OWN LAW AND HIS FAVOURITE GAME DISAGREE HERE, and naming that is the job. What ports is the shape applied to things that are NOT required: the graffiti, the faction tags, the radio, the parts of the valley that are atmosphere. Never a quest step, never a name, never a direction.

looked at through: meta UI (Fagerholt & Lorentzon) · the fiction axis · seen on: dialogue, everywhere

FFX.W03 REFUSE

THERE IS ALMOST NO HUD, BECAUSE THERE IS ALMOST NO DECISION

Walking around Spira there is essentially nothing on screen. No minimap, no compass, no health bar, no quest marker. FFX is famous for it.

WHY IT WORKS It can afford that because FFX is a CORRIDOR. There is no world map for most of the game. The level does the navigating, so the interface does not have to.

REFUSE · WHAT WE DO Bohemia is an open valley of 27+ districts and he has already reported being "launched into a random part of the city" and walking through it lost. A clean empty screen is not a style you choose, IT IS SOMETHING A CORRIDOR PAYS FOR. If we copy the empty screen without the corridor we get a beautiful HUD over a player who has no idea where he is. We have to EARN the empty screen with landmarks and light, not declare it. Anyone who quotes "FFX has no HUD" at this project without quoting this paragraph is quoting half a finding.

looked at through: non-diegetic minimisation (Fagerholt & Lorentzon) · seen on: the world

FFX.W04 REFUSE

THE TEXT BOX IS THIN BECAUSE THE PERFORMANCE IS THE CONTENT

FFX was the first Final Fantasy with voice acting. The characters are on screen, lit and acting, and the subtitle is a thin band at the bottom that gets out of the way.

WHY IT WORKS The box is small because the box is not carrying the scene. The actors are.

REFUSE · WHAT WE DO WE HAVE NO VOICE ACTING AND WILL NOT HAVE ANY. Every ounce of the performance in Bohemia is carried by the words and by a 112px pixel face. So our dialogue sheet must be the OPPOSITE of FFX's: bigger, with the speaker's face IN it, with room for the line to breathe, which is what the run already does. Copying FFX's thin band here would be copying the consequence of a budget we do not have. The current sheet is right and this study says so.

looked at through: the fiction axis (Fagerholt & Lorentzon) · clarity (Hodent) · seen on: dialogue

MP.W01 TAKE

NOWHERE TO REST

Brutalism is his named environment inspiration, and the stated reason is behavioural rather than visual: the player never really feels like they can rest anywhere. His work is described as taking after the relentlessness of military organisations.

WHY IT WORKS A level rule, not a texture rule. The building refuses you a corner to sit in, and that does more work than any amount of grime.

TAKE · WHAT WE DO It is the exact counterweight to FFX.W01, the save point you walk to. Bohemia needs BOTH: a valley where almost nowhere is safe, and a small number of places that are, which you can see from a distance because somebody is keeping the lights on there. Nowhere to rest is what makes a save sphere mean something. Together they are danger by place and light equals territory, already both law.

looked at through: the fiction axis (Fagerholt & Lorentzon) · seen on: the world

MP.W02 ADAPT

THE SOUND IS THE OTHER HALF, NOT A LAYER ON TOP

Reviewers of Machine Party keep crediting the audio for the atmosphere, and Alex Peipman's score is called out for a grimy, oppressive consistency that deliberately contrasts with how silly some of the minigames are. Klubnika scores most of his own work.

WHY IT WORKS In this family of games the industrial audio is not decoration over the art direction, it is a second channel carrying the same claim.

ADAPT · WHAT WE DO Bohemia has a rack of hundreds of cooked instruments and a 120 BPM law that everything quantises to, so the second channel exists and is further along than the first. But this lane owns ui_deny and the shared rule underneath it: a sound may be the best copy of a message and never the only copy. Klubnika can lean on audio because he is not shipping to a phone on silent in a bright room.

looked at through: signs and feedback (Hodent) - meta (Fagerholt & Lorentzon) · seen on: every screen

MP.W03 TAKE

FINAL FANTASY 10 MEETS MACHINE PARTY, AND THE SEAM IS THE POINT

His own words on 8/27, and it is the first time anybody has named what the Bohemia look actually is. Two games at opposite ends of the same book: one is a readable list of numbers laid over a soft tropical world, the other is a filthy steel object with almost no numbers on it at all.

WHY IT WORKS They are not opposites, they are two halves of one answer. Final Fantasy 10 is right about INFORMATION: do the arithmetic for the player and show the answer. Machine Party is right about SUBSTANCE: the thing carrying the information should look like it was welded, not designed. What kills most interfaces is having one without the other, either a beautiful object you cannot read or a clean readout with no character in it at all.

TAKE · WHAT WE DO It is already what his 8/27 verdict describes and he may not have noticed he was describing it. THE CUT CORNER is a stamped metal tag, which is Machine Party. THE HEAVY LINE is a thing that was welded rather than drawn, which is Machine Party. GOLD AND COLD is two colours that MEAN two things, you and the machine, which is Final Fantasy 10's discipline exactly. ALL TYPEWRITER WIDTH is a readout on a device, which is both at once. And the dirt died because grime belongs to the room and not to the readout, which is the seam holding. THE LOOK HE PICKED IS ALREADY THE SENTENCE HE SAID, and the next thing built goes on this test: is it readable like Final Fantasy 10, and is it made of something like Machine Party. If it fails either half it is not Bohemia.

looked at through: consistency (Hodent) - the fiction axis (Fagerholt & Lorentzon) · seen on: all of them

Every one of these has a code like FFX.R01. That is not decoration. Any time somebody around here says "let us do it like Final Fantasy", they have to say which one, and the machine checks that it is real.

✓ROUND TWO

MACHINE PARTY. You did not vote on my three games, you just said the answer, which is better. Fourteen findings above, mixed in with the Final Fantasy ones.

The dossier we already had on Machine Party was about the WORLD, and nobody had ever opened it for the interface, even though its own section is called THE MACHINE IS THE INTERFACE. That section is this round.
